=== Overview ===
[[File:Bessho Suwa Jinja Keidai.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds of Suwa Shrine|250px]]
The date of establishment is unknown, but there exists a {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|zh|上樑記牌|qid=Q8008834}} (ridgepole inscription) dating from {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 12{{sfn|Ashida, ed.|1930|p=272}}. There is a theory identifying this shrine with the “Izumo no Yashiro” recorded in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}} and the “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Izumo Shrine}}” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}{{sfn|Ashida, ed.|1930|p=272}}, but there are multiple candidate shrines for Izumo no Yashiro / Izumo Shrine, and criticism of the Suwa Shrine theory is strong{{sfn|Ishizuka|1986|pp=156–189}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5 (1872), it was designated a village shrine{{sfn|Takahashi|1983|p=515}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
'''{{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Kami}}'''
:According to the 18th-century topographical work {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Unyōshi}}, there was a rock cliff more than 40 ken high on Mount Miya, and beside it a round standing rock about 30 ken high and roughly 5 jō in circumference, called “Hobashira-ishi” or “{{ruby|檣|kachi|rp1=[|rp2=]}}-ishi”{{sfn|Ashida, ed.|1930|p=272}}{{efn|The Hobashira-ishi no longer exists{{sfn|Shimane Prefectural Shrine Association}}.}}. There is a tradition that when the monk Chishun, who founded {{ill|Gakuen-ji|ja|鰐淵寺|qid=Q11674322}} located near Suwa Shrine, came from {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}}, three old men welcomed him by boat and then divided the ship’s fittings and flew off to three places{{sfn|Ashida, ed.|1930|p=272}}. One of them was Suwa Myōjin; the fitting he took was the mast, which is said to be the Hobashira-ishi{{sfn|Ashida, ed.|1930|p=272}}.

'''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yatsukamizuomitsuno-no-Mikoto}}'''
:The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Unyōshi}} states “it is Takeminakata-no-Mikoto,” and does not list Yatsukamizuomitsuno-no-Mikoto{{sfn|Ashida, ed.|1930|p=271}}.
